item.title: Re: Does the Black Moon Howl?
item.content:encoded: My headcanon is that it's a general-purpose memetic identifier. There are various code response-phrases that are given in various situations, and each Foundation staff member is implanted with the basic memetic trigger when they're first employed — they can be half-dead, but as long as they still have vocal cords and a brain, they'll involuntarily respond with a phrase that corresponds to their job, clearance level, and department. In this way, it can also be used as a kind of password system; only people who respond in a certain way will be granted access to the file, and since it's implanted in your head, it's impossible to cheat.

item.title: Re: Does the Black Moon Howl?
item.content:encoded: In most tales I've read, it's used by the upper echelons of the Foundation as a password.

item.title: Re: Does the Black Moon Howl?
item.content:encoded:
As I understand it, it doesn't have an 'appropriate' response. It exploits some sort of side effect common to most memetic infections and lasting cognitohazards. The 'appropriate' response is 'No' or 'What?' or 'I don't understand.' Someone who's infected by a memetic agent will instead reflexively make some mystically nonsensical response.
There is no Black Moon, and it doesn't Howl. It's not even a method used in formal research because it doesn't always work. But out in the field, if you suspect something's messing with your partner's head and you don't have a solid enough reason to justify taking them back for evaluation, you can say it as a quick-and-dirty test.

Imagine a Keter skip that has no visible symptoms, except for that it makes all its infectees hop when they hear someone snapping their fingers. So obviously, the Foundation's going to snap its fingers around people they think are infected.

item.title: Re: Does the Black Moon Howl?
item.content:encoded:
I like to think that the 'Black Moon' is code for some crazy anomaly that is inside the moon, and will howl to signify some sort world-changing/ending event. Only the 05s know about it, as it first howled to the original 05s who would then tell their successors about it, along with a pass-phrase for each of them. Now, the Black Moon is largely forgotten except for it being used as a passcode. But someday, the Black Moon will howl again.

If I had any writing ability I'd make this a tale, but alas, I don't.

item.title: Re: Does the Black Moon Howl?
item.content:encoded:
It comes, I believe from SCP-257-ARC. It was intended, I think, to be a shiboleth, and is mostly used in this way where it shows up again.

There's no one real world definition of "black moon" and it isn't an established astronomical term-of-art. Depending on the source, black moons can be:

  • The second new moon in the same month.
  • The third new moon in a season of four new moons.
  • No new moon in February.
  • No full moon in February.

The moon, as it interacts with the Earth's magnetic field, with solar radiation and cosmic radiation can produce or reflect many different electromagnetic signals, and can be said to be howling at times.

item.title: Does the Black Moon Howl?
item.content:encoded:
I have always been familiar with the common phrase that seems to show up often on the site, that being "Does the Black Moon Howl?"

I am aware that there are a few responses to the question and what I know so far are:

  • "Only to startle the Sun."
  • "When the Foundation crumbles."
  • "Only when waning"

Are there more responses?

Also, let's discuss the actual question/phrase. What is the Black Moon originally, is it intended as something in particular, and which article used the term first? Any personnel headcanons about the phrase? I would like to hear some.
